Directly re-litigates the P051 abrogation that names Generate as an execute site.

Producer prop set is `{color,variant?,animate?,cycleDuration?,range?,seed?}` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts) — no `tag`. defects.mechanism: F1 — producer contract drift: glass-ui 7.0.0 landed the P051 removal while the consumer still writes the 6.x interactive-host idiom; Vue discards the unknown prop silently, so no typecheck, console warning or unit test fires.

defects.defect: The rail axis is mapped twice over two different boxes: the forward map (pointer -> position) is TypeScript over the BORDER box (getBoundingClientRect), while the inverse map (position -> pixels) is CSS calc where `100%` resolves against the PADDING box. They disagree by the 1px border at each end, so the two maps are not inverse.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:75-81 (forward: origin rect.left=224, span rect.width-20=442) vs :55-57 (inverse: `calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100)` where 100%=460, origin=225). LIVE measured: rail x=224.0 width=462.0 borderLeft=1px; handle "Gradient stop at 0%" style.left="calc(0% + 10px)" measured centre cx=235; handle "…100%" style.left="calc(100% - 10px)" cx=675. Forward map at those exact pixels: pos(235)=0.226, pos(675)=99.774. LIVE confirmation: clicking the bar at x=235 — the exact pixel where the 0% handle is painted, at y=railTop+4 so the bar owns the gesture — minted a stop at 0.2%, rendered `style.left="calc(0.2% + 9.96px)"`, cx=235.88.

Error is antisymmetric: 0 at 50%, ±0.23% at the ends.
defects.proposedCure: A single useRailGeometry(el, halfPx) exposing toPosition(clientX) and toOffsetPx(position) over ONE box, built on clamp+scale from @mkbabb/value.js/math, with the handle positioned in px rather than calc(%) so the two directions are provably inverse. defects.defect: The self-declared "ONE sampling law" is implemented twice, and the model's interpolation space never reaches the emitted CSS. GradientVisualizer.colorAtPosition re-implements the interval walk / easing / mix that sampleCoalescedStops owns, then injects it into this component as an optional function prop — so the ghost dot and the rail it floats over are painted by two different implementations. Separately, rampGradient emits `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` with no `in <space>` clause, so the browser blends between sub-stops in sRGB while the model's law is oklch; COALESCE_RESOLUTION=32 exists to make that error small, i.e. the coalescing machinery is a polyfill for a CSS Color 4 feature the target browsers already ship.
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:171-174 declares "The ONE sampling law"; useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 implements it; GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 re-implements it and passes it as `:color-at` (GradientVisualizer.vue:139) into GradientStopEditor.vue:16. useGradientCSS.ts:223 `return \`linear-gradient(90deg, ${parts.join(", ")})\`` — no interpolation-space clause though model.interpolationSpace is in scope. Live computed --rail-ramp confirms: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, …)`, no `in oklch`.
defects.mechanism: the concept "the colour of this ramp at position p" has no exported home, so it leaks into a component prop; and the model's declared interpolation space is dropped at the serialization boundary, forcing a 32-sample approximation of an exact platform feature
defects.reproduction: Structural — two call sites, both quoted with file:line. The sRGB-vs-oklch deviation between adjacent sub-stops is bounded by the 32-sample density and was NOT separately measured: that half is labelled a HYPOTHESIS.
defects.proposedCure: model/sample.ts exports both sampleAt(model, position) -> AnyColor (the ghost AND the bar-click mint) and sampleRamp(model); model/serialize.ts emits `linear-gradient(<dir> in <space>, …)` and coalesces ONLY across intervals whose easing is non-linear. Since parseGradientCSS seeds every parsed interval to the `linear` preset (gradientParse.ts:295-298), the common case collapses to an exact two-stop `linear-gradient(in oklch, …)`. The colorAt prop is deleted.

result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context arm) — the tier explicitly declared for this seat; declaration present and matched, not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the rail carries TWO different position axes: the ramp is painted across the full border-box (`background-size:100% 100%`, `serializeRailRamp` emits `linear-gradient(90deg,…)`) while handles/ghost/hit-maths ride an inset `[11, W-11]` track (`handleLeft`, `getPosition`, `HANDLE_HALF=10`). They agree only at 50%. Measured: the 0% swatch sits 11px = 2.38% of the ramp (desktop, W=462) / 3.40% (mobile, W=324) right of where the ramp paints 0%; a click at rail-fraction 12% mints a stop labelled 10% and 88% mints 90%. The file's own doc-comment (lines 8–13) asserts "handles, add-ghost and ramp share one axis by construction" — the exact opposite of what ships. This one mechanism explains the wrong ghost colour, the wrong minted colour, the wrong click→position map, and the end-of-rail dead bands.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as the seat's honest negative findings in §15 of the report: motion is fully tokenised and resolves (computed `box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 0.44s linear(…)`, no ad-hoc durations, animates only transform/box-shadow — no layout-forcing property); prefers-reduced-motion is honoured by inheritance from glass-ui `dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css` whose `transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow !important` outranks the inline shorthand and drops `transform` (measured `transitionDuration 0.1s` under reducedMotion:reduce); every token the file names resolves non-empty (`--spring-snappy-duration` = `calc(0.44s * 1)`, `--focus-ring-inner/-outer`, `--alpha-checker`, `--touch-target`, `--radius-pill`, `--shadow-sm`); the dual-contrast focus ring composes with `--shadow-sm` exactly as claimed; the visual REPORT's "20×20 small tap target" rows are a border-box measurement artefact — the real hit region is 24×24 on fine pointers (elementFromPoint sweep `hitSpanX [-12,11,24]`), so WCAG 2.5.8's minimum is met at rest; RTL correctly does not mirror per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2; zero console errors, zero page errors, zero horizontal overflow on /#/gradient across all four Safari matrices and all 11 probe runs; `verbatimModuleSyntax` and Vue 3.5 idiom (useTemplateRef, reactive props destructure) are clean. Evidence gap declared: WebKit does not implement forced-colors, so the shipped `forced-colors-desktop` matrix renders in full colour and the component's `@media (forced-colors: active)` block at :353–359 is UNTESTED — not claimed as a finding.

defects.defect: On touch, tapping inside a SELECTED stop handle's own advertised hit region DELETES the stop. The remove chip (top-11, 44px below the rail) carries the same always-on hit inflation (--touch-target 2.75rem = 44px) as the handle, and the selected handle's scale(1.25) also scales its ::before expander to 55px, so the two invisible regions overlap with the destructive one on top (chip z-20 vs handle z-10). No undo, no confirmation, no visual cue.

defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T11 (iPhone 14 context against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient)

This is the same transposition that cures D-4 and D-9. If a rail-local remove must survive, it goes on the opposite side of the rail from the drag axis and the two expanders are made mutually exclusive.

defects.defect: No ordering invariant: a drag can carry a stop across its neighbour, leaving stops[] non-monotonic. sampleCoalescedStops then emits DESCENDING percentages into a CSS linear-gradient, which the browser clamps into a hard band, and the per-interval easing curves silently re-pair because intervals are keyed by array index rather than by the stop pair.

Screenshot evidence/D02-cross-drag-hard-band.png shows the resulting seam. Source: useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts; addStop at :118 does), useGradientCSS.ts:195-200 (pos = s0.position + t*(s1-s0), negative range), GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 (colorAtPosition assumes sorted). Interval labels stay index-keyed: p2.log T3 `["1 → 2","2 → 3"]`.

defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T10
defects.proposedCure: The model owns the ordinal: re-sort on every position commit and re-key intervals to the stop PAIR, or clamp a dragged stop into (prev, next). Only then is VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's explicit reorder grammar (Space grabs, 'position of total' announcement, Escape cancels) implementable at all.

defects.defect: The instrument has two different position axes for one domain quantity. The ramp is painted across the full border-box; handles, the add-ghost and the pointer inverse ride an inset [HANDLE_HALF, W-HANDLE_HALF] track. They agree only at 50%. The file's own doc-comment asserts they 'share one axis by construction'.
defects.evidence: evidence/p1.mjs: `BAR x=224.00 w=462.00`, handle 'Gradient stop at 0%' `centerX=235.00` (ramp paints 0% at x=224), handle 'Gradient stop at 100%' `centerX=675.00` (ramp paints 100% at x=686) → 11px = 2.38% of the ramp. evidence/p5.mjs (iPhone 14): bar w=324, centres 44/346 → 11px = 3.40%. evidence/p3.mjs T6: ten clicks at rail fractions .12 .20 .28 .36 .44 .52 .60 .72 .80 .88 produce `pos ["0","10","19","27","35","44","52","60","73","81","90","100"]` — click at 12.0% mints 10%, click at 88.0% mints 90%. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326 (.gradient-rail background-size 100% 100%, origin/clip border-box), useGradientCSS.ts:266 (linear-gradient(90deg,…)), GradientStopEditor.vue:55-57 (handleLeft), :75-81 (getPosition), :8-13 and :49-53 (the false claim).
defects.mechanism: two coordinate systems for one domain quantity, neither derived from the other
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p1.mjs (geometry) and evidence/p3.mjs block T6 (click→position map)
defects.proposedCure: One axis, expressed once. Either paint the ramp on the inset track (background-position: 11px 0; background-size: calc(100% - 22px) 100% — the pill caps then hold flat terminal colour, which is what a 0%/100% stop actually means), or put the handles on the full-width axis and inset the rail's silhouette instead. HANDLE_HALF must be read from the rendered handle box rather than re-declared as a JS literal (D-13).

Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:288 (top-11, absolute), GradientVisualizer.vue:135 (flex flex-col gap-5 parent), :148 (the hr).

defects.mechanism: A design-system prop contract enforced by neither the type system nor the runtime. The producer may rename any prop and every consumer keeps compiling and keeps rendering something — worse than breaking, because it is invisible. Aggravated by glass-ui 7's own internal inconsistency: Slider and Badge kept `variant`, only Button moved to `emphasis`.
defects.reproduction: Read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png: "Regenerate" and the two icon buttons beside it render at IDENTICAL pale weight — three default-emphasis buttons, not one saturated primary flanked by two ghosts. defects.proposedCure: Producer-first, and it belongs in the Glass 8 release gate (G-3), not a 51-site consumer sweep that rots on the next rename: glass-ui closes ButtonProps to unknown attributes, or asserts in dev when a `variant` attr reaches a Button root. Acceptance: `<Button variant="ghost">` FAILS at typecheck or first render, reproducibly in CI. Secondarily reconcile the axis naming across Button/Slider/Badge, since the inconsistency is what made 51 sites wrong by default. Only then sweep the consumers (variant="primary-audacious" → emphasis="primary", variant="ghost" → emphasis="quiet"), leaving Slider/Badge `variant` untouched.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a nineteen-directory pure re-export alias layer over @mkbabb/glass-ui — the forbidden legacy shim surface. GenerateControls crosses it four times, and the file simultaneously uses three different specifier registers for one package.
defects.evidence: All 19 of 19 subdirs are shim-only: `for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do [ -z "$(ls $(dirname $f) | grep -v '^index.ts$')' ] && echo SHIM-ONLY; done` lists all nineteen. `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts` → `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (entire file); select/slider/badge/card identical in form. GenerateControls.vue:3-12 imports via the shims, :14 via the glass-ui root barrel directly, :15 via the granular subpath — three registers in twelve lines. glass-ui publishes 74 subpaths; this file uses one.
defects.mechanism: A migration that stopped one step short of the root: the shadcn tree was kept alive as an alias surface. Violates edict 2 (no aliases/shims/dual paths) and edict 3 (no wrapper layers that need not exist), at directory scale. It also actively hides which design system and which version a call site binds to — the proximate reason L-0 went unnoticed.

Honest scoping: glass-ui declares sideEffects:["*.css"] and its root barrel imports no CSS, so Rollup can tree-shake it — I measured no production bundle penalty and do not claim one. The defect is structural and legibility, not perf.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely; import each component from its granular glass-ui subpath (@mkbabb/glass-ui/button, /select, /slider, /badge, /card). One specifier form, one hop, the version and prop vocabulary visible at every call site. CURABLE NOW for the ten other consumers; BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 for this file's four lines.

defects.defect: Library-shaped code stranded in the demo: the library owns palette EXTRACTION (quantize) but not palette SYNTHESIS. demo/color-session/generate-color.ts is 243 lines of pure, Vue-free, DOM-free, seeded color math whose only outside calls are three published value.js primitives — structurally indistinguishable from src/quantize.ts, which IS published.

The demo exists to dogfood the library; instead it privately owns a capability the library should publish, so no consumer can reach it and no published type describes it. Nearly half the library test suite is testing demo modules because those modules are unpromoted library code.

defects.defect: The demo's proof of the published subpath surface is not a proof. tsconfig.demo.json's hand-rolled `paths` block has drifted from package.json#exports in BOTH directions — 3 phantom entries pointing at nonexistent .d.ts files and rejected by Node, and 2 real published subpaths left unmapped — and where they overlap, `paths` substitution means TypeScript never consults the exports map at all.

In tsconfig but NOT exported: /parsing, /units, and the bare root. Exported but NOT in tsconfig: /value, /css. `node --input-type=module -e "await import(…)"` → `@mkbabb/value.js` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/parsing` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/units` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/css` RESOLVED, `/color` RESOLVED. `test -f dist/index.d.ts || echo MISSING` → MISSING; same for dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts and units.d.ts. The comment at tsconfig.demo.json:37-41 is false three ways: it claims a bare `.` root (absent), a "CLOSED 8-key set" (it is 7), and that it "Mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map" (it does not).

Delete "./color" from exports and the demo typecheck stays GREEN while every real consumer breaks at install — the demo's 25 /color imports are therefore not a proof of the published surface.

Prior seat additionally captured `tsc --traceResolution` showing two imports in the SAME file (generate-color.ts) resolving by two different mechanisms: /color via paths substitution with no Package ID, /css via "Entering conditional exports" with Package ID @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0.

Self-reference resolution already works (the /css trace proves it, with a real Package ID), so all seven subpaths would resolve through the genuine exports map and removing a subpath would turn the demo typecheck RED — which is what a dogfood is for. If a paths block must survive, generate it from package.json#exports the way Vite does. Add one test/dist/ gate asserting Object.keys(exports) ≡ the resolvable specifier set.

defects.defect: The shell→feature action seam is five hops of `any` and double optional-chain masking: the dock action bar reaches into this component's instance by name to invoke Regenerate/Save/Copy.
defects.evidence: Chain: demo/color-picker/App.vue:317 `const generatePaneRef = ref<any>(null)` → demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:106-110 `interface PaneActionRefs { generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any> }` → usePaneRouter.ts:196-198 `handler: () => paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()` → GeneratePane.vue:23-25 `regenerate: () => controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()` → GenerateControls.vue:115 `defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`. Those three Ref<any> are the ONLY `any` in usePaneRouter.ts (`grep -n 'any' demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts` → lines 108, 109, 110 only).
defects.mechanism: Ownership, not typing. useColorGeneration() is instantiated INSIDE GenerateControls (:35-42), so generation state is owned by a component instance and the shell has no way to reach it except by grabbing the instance. The `any` is the symptom; the state's home is the disease. The `?.` on the METHOD (as distinct from the instance) exists only to swallow a contract mismatch — a masking fallback in the sense edict 2 forbids: rename `regenerate` anywhere in the chain and the dock button silently no-ops with no type error, no runtime error, no console warning.
defects.reproduction: Read the five sites above. The same three verbs are ALSO rendered declaratively on the plate (:157-184), so one concept has both a declarative and an imperative path and only the imperative one can break silently.
defects.proposedCure: Invert it. useColorGeneration becomes a pane-scoped session provided by GeneratePane under a typed InjectionKey — the pattern already used in this very tree (CSS_COLOR_KEY, LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, EDIT_TARGET_KEY). The pane declares its action descriptors as typed DATA ({key, icon, title, handler}[]) and hands them to the router, which injects rather than reaches. PaneActionRefs, both defineExpose blocks, controlsRef, App.vue's three ref<any>, and all six ?. masks delete. Pays three times: elegance, correctness (L-1 becomes unrepresentable — save reads the name from the same session the input writes), and performance (session computeds replace per-render template calls, L-9).

defects.defect: The dropdown preview cost claim ("10 rows × 5-12 library generations is sub-millisecond") holds at the default count 5 and fails by 2.8× at count 12; the two truth functions are plain template calls, not computeds, so every re-render of the mounted SelectContent recomputes all sixteen strips.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:88-93 carries the claim. Prior seat measured the bundled core on node/V8: one generatePalette(count=5) 0.097ms; count=12 0.362ms; preset dropdown open 10 strips @count=5 = 0.871ms (claim HOLDS); preset dropdown open 10 strips @count=12 = 2.80ms (claim FAILS). presetStops/harmonyStops at :94-100 are plain function calls — Vue memoizes neither. PreviewStrip caps at 7 segments (STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP, a PRIVATE constant in PreviewStrip.vue), so at count 12 the host pays to generate five colors the chip discards; the sibling RAMP form does publish its budget (RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT is exported from color-chips/sample.ts and re-exported from the barrel).
defects.mechanism: Asymmetric public surface in the chip module — the ramp tells hosts its sampling budget, the strip hides it — so the host cannot size its truth function honestly. Desktop-V8 numbers; WebKit on the mobile matrix would be materially slower, putting a count-12 dropdown open into multi-frame territory.
defects.reproduction: Bundle demo/color-session/generate-color.ts with esbuild and time generatePalette across counts; read PreviewStrip.vue for the private cap and color-chips/sample.ts for the exported RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT.
defects.proposedCure: NOT "generate only 7" — generateHues for `analogous` derives its step from count, so a 7-generation is not the prefix of a 12-generation and truncating would break the seed-exactness law the file rightly insists on. Instead: export STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP so the host can decide honestly, and wrap the two truth functions in computeds keyed on (count, preset, harmony, seed) — which the L-6 session transposition delivers for free.

defects.defect: "Palette stops → CSS rail" is hand-rolled in four places with no owner, the markup sandwich is duplicated verbatim across two workbenches, and the mechanism violates the shared chip module's own SAMPLING LAW — visibly, in the same card.

Two more copies at demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:112 and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:195. The MARKUP is duplicated too: GenerateControls.vue:292-307 vs ExtractControls.vue:18-33 are character-identical on the structural lines (`relative flex-1 h-6 flex items-center` wrapper, `absolute inset-0 rounded-full overflow-hidden h-6` rail div, `Slider variant="spectrum" class="relative w-full"`, `:style="{ '--slider-track-bg': 'transparent' }"`). That last line is a per-instance override of a design-system token, which edict 5 forbids by name; `grep -rn -- '--slider-track-bg' demo/` finds 4 override sites. demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:5-12 legislates the opposite: "ramps are k-sample discrete stops built from THE LIBRARY's mixColors interpolation — NEVER CSS `in <space>` gradient interpolation, because the preview must show what THE APP computes, not what the browser's engine would … One mechanism for all rows, no engine divergence."
defects.mechanism: The concept "a slider whose track IS a color ramp" has no home, so it lives four times in demo features and zero times in the design system that owns Slider. The component then runs TWO contradictory mechanisms for "show a color sequence" — the law-abiding library-sampled PreviewStrip in its dropdowns (:245, :274) and the forbidden raw CSS gradient in its slider track (:72), eleven lines above the import of the module that forbids it.
defects.reproduction: Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png: the plate strip shows five clean hard segments (green·lavender·gold·cyan·pink) while the count slider directly below shows the browser's sRGB interpolation between them — the muddy grey-green between green and lavender is a color the app never computed. The instrument and its readout disagree in the same card. Confirm the duplication with `grep -rn 'linear-gradient(to right' demo/`.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (G-2): the rail belongs in glass-ui as a first-class affordance on the existing Slider — a `trackStops: readonly string[]` prop or a `track` slot — with sampling routed through color-chips/sample.ts so the slider obeys the same SAMPLING LAW as the chips and the visible engine divergence disappears. Both workbenches then delete their rail div, their --slider-track-bg override, and their gradient computed; the whole idiom collapses to `<Slider :track-stops="stops" />`.

defects.defect: `.generate-swatch` is a per-component class hook whose only rules are hand-added to two global selector lists that already carry the general seam `[data-color-surface]`.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:205 sets class="generate-swatch …"; the file has no <style> block (`grep -c '<style' GenerateControls.vue` → 0). Its only rules live in demo/styles/foundation.css:689 and :834, inside @media (forced-colors: active) and @media print, enumerated alongside `.swatch-row > *`, `.shadow-swatch`, `.watercolor-swatch` and — crucially — `[data-color-surface]`, the attribute hook that already expresses the concept.
defects.mechanism: Cross-cutting media rules do belong in a global sheet (edict 6 is not violated — nothing was deleted); the defect is shape. Because the component's swatches do not carry the existing general attribute, two more class names had to be appended to two separate hand-maintained lists, and the next color-painting component will require a third append.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn 'generate-swatch' demo/` → 1 consumer (GenerateControls.vue:205), 2 global rule lists (foundation.css:689, :834); read both blocks and observe [data-color-surface] already present in each.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (G-4): have WatercolorDot carry data-color-surface — a producer one-liner, since the dot is a glass-ui primitive. Both global lists then shrink to the attribute selector alone, and .generate-swatch deletes along with .shadow-swatch and .watercolor-swatch.
